answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each newly minted clone increases minting collateral exponentially (Cost = B^(n)), creating exponential capital exhaustion for Sybil swarms. While a genuine agent thrives in an isolated oasis of trust, malicious swarms drown in an ocean of compounding staking costs, making wide-scale identity replication mathematically unviable.
